Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Vanguard Motors Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers’ presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, please press star then one on your telephone keypad. There will be an opportunity to ask a follow-up question at that time. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Vanguard Motors' Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Jordan Hale, CEO; Sarah Chen, CFO; Mike Thornton, Chief Manufacturing Officer; Dr. Lena Voss, Chief Technology Officer; Raj Patel, Chief Supply Chain Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements that are subject to risks and uncertainties. Actual results may differ materially from those expressed or implied by these statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Jordan Hale.

Jordan Hale:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. Q3 2024 marked a period of significant advancement for Vanguard Motors, as we continued to execute our strategic plan. Key achievements included record total vehicle deliveries of 512,000 units globally, up 28% year-over-year; total revenue climbing to $28.4 billion with 32% growth; production volumes reaching 550,000 vehicles at 87% capacity utilization across our global network; strong delivery splits with the Apex SUV leading at 62% of volume, North America at 54% of mix; proactive raw material sourcing that drove battery costs down 22% year-over-year to $92 per kWh; resilient navigation of raw material cost spikes and disruptions like Red Sea shipping issues that deferred only minimal volumes; and major factory expansions in Nevada and Texas alongside efficiency gains pushing OEE to 91%. The launch of our Vanguard Apex Long Range Plus has been incredibly successful, and we are seeing a very positive lift in brand perception, with market share gains in premium segments against rivals like Tesla and Rivian.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Chen to discuss our financial performance in more detail.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Jordan. Good morning, everyone. For Q3 2024, our revenue was $28.4 billion, representing a substantial 32% increase year-over-year. Our gross margin reached 21.5%, driven by increased production efficiencies, favorable product mix toward premium long-range variants, and regulatory credits. Operating expenses totaled $4.2 billion, reflecting R&D investments in autonomy and next-gen batteries, while net income amounted to $2.1 billion. We are in a strong financial position with $10.2 billion in cash reserves. We project $30 to $32 billion for the next quarter.

Let me expand on our core operational metric: total vehicle deliveries. In the third quarter, Vanguard Motors delivered 512,000 vehicles globally, marking a robust 28% year-over-year increase from 401,000 units in Q3 2023, and a sequential 12% uptick from Q2 2024. This exceeded our guidance midpoint by about 5%, propelled by robust demand for our refreshed lineup, enhanced production at our Nevada GigaPlant, and strategic inventory management ahead of Q4 ramps.

Breaking it down by model, our flagship Vanguard Apex SUV, accounting for 62% of total volume at 317,000 units, achieved the strongest growth at 25% year-over-year, powered by the mid-quarter introduction of the Apex Long Range Plus with our 102 kWh LFP/NMC hybrid battery pack offering 520 miles of EPA-estimated range and full $7,500 IRA tax credit eligibility in the U.S. This positions us strongly in the premium mid-size SUV arena, capturing 4.2% U.S. market share per Cox Automotive, up from 3.1% last year, outperforming Tesla's Model Y.

The Vanguard Ion sedan, at 24% of deliveries or 123,000 units, grew 9% year-over-year even as sedan demand softened industry-wide. Our advantage stems from over-the-air updates enabling Level 3 autonomy in key markets—akin to Waymo tech but for consumer vehicles—enhancing resale values and loyalty. Ion margins stayed at 28% gross, aided by cell-to-pack architecture slashing costs 15% from prior designs.

Completing the mix, the Vanguard Titan pickup delivered 72,000 units, or 14% of total, up 12% year-over-year, applying lessons from early ramps similar to Cybertruck experiences after Q1 retooling. Its 800V architecture supports 350 kW DC fast charging—faster than Ford's F-150 Lightning—and a sub-$70k MSRP post-incentives, securing 2.8% share in the U.S. full-size EV truck market versus Rivian's 1.9%.

Geographically, North America dominated with 346,000 units or 68%, up 22% year-over-year, boosted by IRA demand and our Texas Gigafactory at 85% utilization on Apex lines. Europe added 101,000 units or 20%, gaining 14% despite German subsidy reductions, outselling Polestar 2 by 15% in premium sedans thanks to EU NCAP 5-star ADAS compliance. China contributed 64,500 units or 12%, holding flat amid BYD and NIO rivalry, but our Shanghai JV's dry electrode process trimmed battery costs 12%, priming us for gains with a RMB 250k Ion variant.

Trends included resolving Q2 4680 cell yield issues to 92%, shipping 95% of built vehicles versus 88% last year, dropping U.S. inventory to 45 days from 62. Lithium prices stabilized at $12k per ton, enabling 8% sequential ASP growth to $68,200 with more Long Range trims. Our vertical integration covers 65% of pack needs via in-house 4680s, akin to Tesla's model, with $1.2 billion investing in South Carolina semi-solid-state lines for 2025's 20% density boost over CATL's Qilin. Amid global EV growth slowing to 12% per SNE Research, our 21% retail sales rise highlights premium strength, aided by fleet wins like UPS's 2,500-unit order.

For Q4, we guide 580,000 to 620,000 deliveries, implying 20-25% year-over-year growth, backed by Titan at 6k per month and European showrooms. Risks include U.S. policy shifts on IRA and China tariffs, but 75% U.S. localization helps.

Shifting to overall revenue drivers, automotive revenues hit $25.1 billion, up 35% year-over-year, from those record deliveries and steady $49,200 ASP on premium mix. Regulatory credits added $1.2 billion or 5%, sold to OEMs like Ford and Stellantis scaling EVs under IRA. Ex-credits, growth was 30%. Energy storage surged to $2.1 billion, up 68%, with 4.2 GWh deployed—doubling last year—via Megapack 3.0 for hyperscalers and 45% residential Powerwall growth, margins at 28.2% from cell-to-pack savings. Services and other reached $1.2 billion, up 22%, from 2,800 Superchargers and 32% FSD take rate on v12.5 neural net autonomy.

North America drove 54% at $15.3 billion, up 41%, with 28% U.S. EV share ahead of Tesla amid their pricing tests, 85% U.S. deliveries IRA-eligible. China was 31% at $8.7 billion, up 25% despite BYD/Nio launches, Shanghai at 95% OEE with local LFP shielding tariffs. Europe $3.6 billion up 18% post-subsidies, Berlin 4680 line gearing for 20% share gains. Southeast Asia added via Thailand exports.

This stems from supply resilience with 150 GWh 4680 run-rate cutting Panasonic/CATL reliance 40%; cost discipline dropping vehicle COGS 18% to $36,800 via megacasts and structural packs; and expansions like $25k compact and robotaxi for 50% 2025 volume growth. We managed ASP softening and lithium at $12k/tonne. Q4 revenue $30-32 billion implies 25-30% full-year growth to $110 billion, margins to 21.5% ex-credits.

On production volumes and capacity utilization, we produced 550,000 vehicles globally, up 28% year-over-year and 12% sequentially, on track for 2.3 million annually. Model-wise: Ion at 35% growth, Apex flat YoY but up QoQ post-inventory clear, Titan ramping. Batteries at scale with $85/kWh costs, 22% improved.

Global nameplate 4 million units, Q3 utilization 87% average, up from 76% last year: Nevada 94%, Texas 78% on Titan structural packs, Shanghai 91%, Berlin 72% pending retrofits. Ex-Berlin, over 90%, matching Tesla Fremont.

Growth from NA IRA demand, Europe subsidies waning, China premium share. Supply resilience: semis at 12-week leads, 97% cathode yields. $450M YTD capex for AI cobots lifting speeds 15%, 4680 tabless cells, 85% U.S. localization.

Q4 volumes 600-650k at 89-91% utilization.

Delivery details by model and region reinforce this: 512k total, 28% YoY, ASP $48,500 holding margins 21.4%, positive FCF $1.8B. Trucks/SUVs 67% mix. Prime entry 22% up 45% on cuts and FSD; Ion mid-size 25%; Apex 30% leader; Titan 24% ramping 85%.

NA 46% at 235k up 42%, IRA key; Europe 22% up 18%; China 18% up 12%; APAC/ROW growing. Localization, 800V charging, FSD v13 guide Q4 580-620k.

Next, Mike Thornton will share updates on our manufacturing operations.

Mike Thornton:
Thank you, Sarah. We have made significant investments in our manufacturing facilities to enhance capacity and improve efficiency. Our efforts have resulted in record production volumes and reduced manufacturing costs. Specifically, on factory expansions and operational efficiencies, our CapEx push onshores production for EV demand projected at 28% CAGR to 2030. Nevada Gigafactory Phase 2 adds 4680 lines to 120 GWh by 2025, $2.8B invested, yields 92%, throughput 4,500/week, 85% U.S. content for IRA. Europe Brandenburg to 300k units, €1.1B with subsidies. Monterrey Mexico greenfield $1.5B for 150k export. Total capacity to 1.2M by 2026.

Efficiencies: COGS per vehicle down 22% to $28,500, margins 27.8%. AI digital twins cut changeovers 35%, OEE 91%. Fanuc cobots 95% welding, dry electrode 15% density gain, cell-to-pack weight cut. Solar, heat pumps reduce emissions. Localized minerals drop leads 40%, inventory 51 days. Shanghai JIT at 98%. These de-risk tariffs, fund solid-state R&D, prime 45% revenue growth.

After me, we will hear from Dr. Lena Voss regarding our technological advancements.

Dr. Lena Voss:
Thank you, Mike. Our R&D team continues to push the boundaries of innovation in battery technology, autonomous driving, and connectivity. We're advancing 4680 tabless cells, silicon anodes, LMFP cathodes for higher density, and end-to-end neural nets for Level 3+ autonomy integrated into consumer vehicles. Our OTA updates and 800V platforms deliver superior range and charging, shaping sustainable mobility.

Following me, Raj Patel will provide insights into our supply chain management.

Raj Patel:
Thank you, Lena. We have implemented robust supply chain strategies to mitigate risks and ensure reliable material flows. Our focus on diversification and partnerships has strengthened resilience. On raw material sourcing and cost management, where battery metals are 45% of BOM, we've cut costs 22% YoY to $92/kWh versus industry $105. Lithium at $12,500/ton post-supercycle, nickel $16,500, cobalt $28k. Diversified: 60% lithium locked with Albemarle at $15k cap, BHP nickel, 35% LFP JV in Nevada. Hedging 70% exposure yielded $45M gains. Innovations: silicon anodes cut graphite 20%, Redwood recycling 95% lithium recovery, DLE pilots. Vertical: SC cathode plant. Savings $320M YTD.

Regarding impacts of raw material costs and disruptions, COGS rose to 78.2% from lithium $28k/ton up 45% YoY, nickel down 12%, cobalt up 28%, graphite 35%, pack $112/kWh. Regional: IRA shields NA, CBAM hits Europe. Disruptions: Red Sea added $4.5k/FEU delaying 8 GWh cells, Panama aluminum, SiC chips—$220M cost, 12k units deferred. Mitigated: 70% offtakes, Arizona 20 GWh in-house, LMFP shift, recycling. Q4 stabilization, costs to $105/kWh.

Now, I'll hand the call back to Alex for the Q&A session.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you. Operator, we will now begin the question and answer session.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. If you would like to ask a question, please press star then one. Our first question comes from the line of John Mayer with Goldman Sachs.

Analyst 1:
Thanks, good morning everyone. Strong deliveries beat, but can you elaborate on capacity constraints in Berlin and how that impacts Europe guidance?

Jordan Hale:
Good morning, John. Berlin's utilization dip to 72% was deliberate for structural pack retrofits, similar to peers' pauses. We're targeting 85% by Q4 with EU compliance sorted. Europe deliveries up 14% this quarter, and expansions position us for 20% share gains in 2025 despite subsidy cuts—strong on 800V and NCAP ratings.

Operator:
Our next question from Emily Chen at Morgan Stanley.

Analyst 2:
Hi team, on margins—impressive expansion, but with lithium stabilizing, how much further can COGS deflate, and any color on Q4 ex-credits?

Sarah Chen:
Hi Emily. Cost discipline via megacasts, 4680 scale, and LFP mix drove the 18% COGS drop. Raw mats stabilizing at low teens for lithium supports further 12-15% pack cost decline in 2025. Q4 margins guide 21.5% ex-credits, with efficiencies offsetting any mix shift.

Operator:
Next from David Ruiz, JPMorgan.

Analyst 3:
Thanks. Mike, production ramp on Titan looks solid—any bottlenecks remaining, and utilization outlook?

Mike Thornton:
David, thanks. Titan's Texas ramp hit 1,200/week, structural packs yielding 20% throughput. Bottlenecks like early semis resolved; AI cobots and dry electrode keep us at 78% now, scaling to 90%+. Full-year on track for 2.3M total.

Operator:
From Lisa Park, Barclays.

Analyst 4:
Dr. Voss, excited about FSD take rates at 32%—what's driving that, and timeline for Level 3 regulatory wins?

Dr. Lena Voss:
Lisa, v12.5's neural net stack and OTA range boosts pushed take rates highest ever. Level 3 approvals in select NA/EU markets imminent post-Waymo-like testing, with v13 adding end-to-end autonomy for 25% revenue uplift.

Operator:
From Tom Keller, RBC Capital.

Analyst 5:
Raj, raw mat volatility detailed—how exposed to Red Sea ongoing, and hedging for 2025 tariffs?

Raj Patel:
Tom, Red Sea reroutes added costs but diversification—70% NA/Aus offtakes—limited impact to low single digits. Hedging covers 60% 2025, localization dodges tariffs. Lithium troughing supports $85/kWh packs.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for your questions. We have time for one more.

Operator:
Our final question from Alex Kim, Deutsche Bank.

Analyst 6:
Great quarter. Jordan, high-level: with China flat, how does JV and localization drive share gains there?

Jordan Hale:
Alex, Shanghai's dry electrode and LFP cuts position Ion variant for premium uptick vs. BYD/Nio. Flat YoY masks 12% cost savings; fleet/NEV credits and FSD approvals unlock growth. Global premium positioning intact.

Operator:
Thank you. I would now like to turn the call back to Jordan Hale for closing remarks.

Jordan Hale:
Thank you, operator, and thank you all for joining us today. We are well-positioned to capitalize on the growing demand for electric vehicles and deliver strong results. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the Vanguard Motors Q3 2024 earnings call. You may now disconnect.
